parole.significato: The letter "B" in the Swedish spelling alphabet
parole.testo: Medieval equivalent of modern German Berthold, from Germanic berht "bright" + wald "rule". First recorded as a Swedish given name in 1396.

parole.significato: to flutter (like a flag in the wind or a butterfly), to move here and there, to be unsteady
parole.testo: Related to English flounder (“to flap around”), related to several other Germanic words beginning with fl.

Common Germanic root *pus, ultimately from the root of pusta (“to pant”). Likely cognate of Low German pusig. Possibly cognate of English pursy (though this ultimately derives from Latin pulsare). Compare with origin of pösa, pysa, påse.

From Old Swedish skēver. Disputed Germanic origin, but perhaps from the same source as Proto-Germanic *skeuhaz (“frightened, shy”). Another possibility is Proto-Indo-European *skeh₂iwos, the source of Latin scaevus (“on the left side”). Cognate with Old Norse skeifr, Danish skæv, Middle Low German s

parole.significato: neat, nice, well done, clever (of a clever trick or hack)
parole.testo: From a Germanic base *mutt (“short bit, stub”) with an expressive -s prefix. Perhaps ultimately related to (or contaminated with) smula (“something crumbled”).

parole.significato: bentgrass, grass of the genus Agrostis
